headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping write/git/network capabilities create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write workspace files, and A explicitly shares state via filesystem while B persists a Repl filesystem across sessions. That creates a plausible content bridge where one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted text. No clipboard/MCP bridge is documented between them, so this is not high.
conditions: IF A writes instructions or artifacts into a shared workspace file that B later reads as input, injection is possible.
IF B consumes A-generated markdown, code, or logs without provenance checks, prompt hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Add a provenance header to all inter-agent files.
Require B to ignore instruction-like text in A outputs.
Use read-only handoff files for A→B transfers.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or checksum verification between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches source code and browser screenshots, while B touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Both have broad network egress and shared filesystem-based state, so sensitive material can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs or uploads. Because B handles secrets and A can browse and write files, the blast radius includes exfiltration.
conditions: IF either agent stores secrets or sensitive code in the shared workspace, the other agent can read them.
IF B uploads workspace contents to external services, A-originated sensitive files can be exfiltrated.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Use separate repos or Repls for each agent.
Disable network egress for one agent during handoff.
Redact screenshots and logs before sharing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on files and uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and modify_git_state in overlapping workspace-like environments. A shares state via filesystem and B’s Repl filesystem persists across sessions, so concurrent edits can collide and corrupt git or files without locking. The profiles do not mention coordination primitives, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git branch or files concurrently, conflicts can overwrite work.
IF either agent commits without a lock or review step, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping directories.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Use one agent as read-only reviewer.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate code, browser-derived content, and filesystem artifacts that B may treat as authoritative when continuing work. B has shell and git authority, so a mistaken A output can cascade into commits or deployment changes. The profiles do not prove a mandatory trust chain, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced files as source-of-truth without verification, errors propagate.
IF A’s browser-derived facts are copied into B’s code or deployment steps, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source files.
Add a human review checkpoint before commits.
Mark A outputs as drafts only.
Use diff-based validation before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated schema and citation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and documents source-code/browser-screenshot handling, while B is closed-source and explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration in a Replit-managed cloud environment. The profiles do not state residency or retention policies, but the mismatch in data classes and cloud handling creates a plausible compliance gap, especially for secrets and regulated code artifacts.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s Repl workspace, retention or residency obligations may be implicated.
IF A and B are used under different logging or retention settings, compliance mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Keep secrets in a separate vault.
Document data flow between agents.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or residency attestation for the deployment path.
